module_title: State Executive - Powers, Ordinances, and Advocate General
introduction: At this level, we dive into the specific constitutional powers of the Governor (like pardoning and issuing ordinances), the constitutional duties of the Chief Minister, and the role of the state's highest law officer, the Advocate General.

core_concepts.title: Pardoning Power (Article 161)
core_concepts.description: The Governor can pardon, remit, commute, or suspend the sentence of any person convicted of an offense against a state law. However, they CANNOT pardon a 'Death Sentence' and have no power regarding Court-Martial (military court) sentences.

core_concepts.title: Ordinance Making Power (Article 213)
core_concepts.description: When the state legislature is not in session, the Governor can issue an Ordinance. It has the same force as a law passed by the assembly. It must be approved by the state legislature within 6 weeks of its reassembly.

core_concepts.title: Duties of the Chief Minister (Article 167)
core_concepts.description: It is the constitutional duty of the CM to communicate all decisions of the council of ministers relating to state administration and legislative proposals to the Governor, and to furnish any information the Governor calls for.

core_concepts.title: Advocate General (Article 165)
core_concepts.description: The highest law officer in the state, appointed by the Governor. They must be qualified to be a High Court judge. They have the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of the state legislature, but NO right to vote.

important_entities.name: State Council of Ministers
important_entities.significance: According to Article 164(2), the state council of ministers is 'collectively responsible' ONLY to the State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha), not to the Legislative Council.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Death Sentence Pardon: President vs. Governor
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A major exception! Even if a death sentence is prescribed under a 'State Law', the power to completely pardon it lies ONLY with the President (Article 72), not the Governor (Article 161).
The Constitution does not lay down any grounds or process of 'impeachment' for the removal of the Governor. The President can remove them at any time.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Swap the first two digits of the President's ordinance article (123) to get the Governor's ordinance article (213).

exam_strategy_tips: Match the Following questions frequently pair Article 161 (Pardoning) and Article 213 (Ordinance) with the Governor's powers.
Remember that the Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
